name: Adoni-bezek
charge: Mutilating seventy kings and feeding them under his table
summary: After the death of Joshua, Judah went up first at the Lord’s word, with Simeon his brother, and slew ten thousand Canaanites and Perizzites in Bezek. Their king fled and was caught, and Judah cut off his thumbs and his great toes. He confessed it himself: seventy kings with their thumbs and great toes cut off had gathered their meat under his table, and as he had done, so God had requited him.
offenseFull: After the death of Joshua the children of Israel asked the Lord who should go up first for them against the Canaanites to fight against them, and the Lord said Judah, for He had delivered the land into his hand; Judah asked Simeon his brother to come up with him into his lot and promised to go with him likewise into Simeon’s, so Simeon went with him (Judges 1:1-3). The Lord delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they slew ten thousand men in Bezek (Judges 1:4). The king who fled from that field had made a practice of mutilation and counted it his glory. He gives the number himself: seventy kings with their thumbs and their great toes cut off had gathered their meat under his table (Judges 1:7). Seventy kings maimed so that they could neither hold a sword nor stand in a rank, kept alive to eat scraps on the floor as a display of his power.

The law of Israel keeps punishment to measure: breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, and as a man causes a blemish in another, so it is done to him (Leviticus 24:19-20; Exodus 21:23-25). Adoni-bezek had exceeded all measure seventy times over.
judgmentFull: They pursued after him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes (Judges 1:6): the same mutilation, once. The record does not soften what Israel did in those wars. When Israel went to war terrible things were done to people, and they were done at the commandment of the Most High and by His measure, and the scripture leaves them in plain sight rather than hiding them. The verdict here is pronounced by the condemned man himself, and the record leaves it in his mouth: as he had done, so God had requited him (Judges 1:7). A Canaanite king read the measure of the God of Israel off his own case and named it justice.

They brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died; and the children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire (Judges 1:7-8). Christ states the rule he fell under as a rule for everyone: with what measure you mete, it will be measured to you again (Matthew 7:2). David dealt with the Ammonites by the same principle when he put the people of their cities under saws and harrows and axes of iron and made them pass through the brickkiln (2 Samuel 12:31), giving back what had been done. And the same measure stands written against the nations that stole a man and sold him: a man who steals a man and sells him, or is found with him in his hand, is to be put to death (Exodus 21:16). That is judgment and justice, and the judgment for it has not been paid.

lawsResolved.text: The restitution and punishment should be according to the crime--Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
If a man causes injury or blemish to another, he shall have the same injury done to him.
Punishment is the fruit and reward for iniquity and wicked ways (you shall reap that which you sow).

text.text: Now after the death of Joshua it came to pass, that the children of Israel asked the Lord, saying, Who shall go up for us against the Canaanites first, to fight against them?
And the Lord said, Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.
And Judah said unto Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with thee into thy lot. So Simeon went with him.
And Judah went up; and the Lord delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand: and they slew of them in Bezek ten thousand men.

And Adoni–bezek said, Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.
And if a man cause a blemish in his neighbour; as he hath done, so shall it be done to him;
Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: as he hath caused a blemish in a man, so shall it be done to him again.
And if any mischief follow, then thou shalt give life for life,
Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
But Adoni–bezek fled; and they pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes.

And Adoni–bezek said, Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.
Now the children of Judah had fought against Jerusalem, and had taken it, and smitten it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.

And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
